1. Claim 4 (Currently Amended): A method of impeding Leishmaniasis transmission in dogs by administering to a dog a composition comprising a Fucose Mannose Ligand (FML) fraction from Leishmania donovani promastigotes or amastigotes and saponin, wherein the method further comprises measuring blocking antibodies in the vaccinated dog that specifically inhibit parasite transmission to sandfly vectors in vitro.

2. Claim 5 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 4, wherein said composition is in the form of a blocking vaccine comprising the FML fraction and saponin formulated to elicit blocking antibodies in canine subjects.

3. Claim 6 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 4, wherein said composition further comprises suitable pharmaceutical vehicles, for blocking Leishmaniasis transmission in dogs, wherein the vaccine efficacy is demonstrated by reduction of parasitemia in vaccinated dogs compared to unvaccinated control dogs.

4. Claim 7 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 4, wherein the Leishmania donovani promastigotes or amastigotes fractions called "Fucose Mannose Ligand" (FML) comprise a glycoprotein complex containing 29% of neutral sugar, 44% of protein, 11% of phosphate and hexoamines traces composed by protein bands with molecular weight ranging from 9 to 95 kDa, some protein bands having carbohydrates at 36 and 54 to 68 kDa, the FML glycidic portion presenting 10% of fucose and 47% of mannose, 30% of glucose, 12% of galactose and xylose traces, amino acids containing 10 to 20% of glutamic acid, alanine, aspartic acid and glycine, 5 to 10% of serine, histidine, lysine, leucine, threonine, proline and valine, and 2 to 5% of arginine, methionine, isoleucine, tyrosine and phenylalanine.
